why: Which runtime can serve which feature, and which reasoning efforts each runtime accepts
(todo/PLAN_one_model_catalog.md, D4). Neither half owns this file: the extension generates
features.consultant, and a file whose lists name an undeclared runtime fails the server's start.
FROZEN to what each half did on 2026-10-04: a runtime is added here when it is added to the product, never
ahead of it. The question consultant's runtimes are not here - shared/runtime-capabilities.json decides them -
and neither is the Bugz ranking list, which is a security allowlist (shared/ranking-vendors.txt), not availability.
effort.source: `list` - the levels below, read off the runtime's own CLI (measuredWith says where);
`probe` - the levels the model's probe report lists (ApiCapabilities.EffortLevels), judged per model;
`unmeasured` - nobody has shown which levels the runtime accepts, so an effort is refused until a measurement
lands (PLAN_one_model_catalog.md D6); `none` - the runtime takes no effort at all.
fastMode.refusesStandard (codex only): the releases, both ends included and compared as numbers, that refuse to be
told the standard tier - they take only `fast` or `flex`, and `service_tier=default` fails the launch at config load
Off row on such a release is sent no tier at all; On still sends `fast`.

effort.note: codex-cli 0.160.0 reads model_reasoning_effort from its config, but no command short of a model turn names the legal values, and its binary carries several look-alike variant lists - so none is written here until one is observed taking effect (E2.2).
The retired Gemini CLI runtime; a row saved on it is moved to antigravity on read (vendors.ts migrateRetired).

effort.measuredWith: claude --help, Claude Code 2.1.289, 2026-10-04: --effort <level> (low, medium, high, xhigh, max)

effort.note: The operator's ruling, 2026-10-04: no effort for Antigravity; the model id carries its level (gemini-3.7-flash-high).
The local module's calibrated capabilities (ApiCapabilities.EffortLevels, COAI_LOCAL_REASONING_EFFORT).

The Team server judges it per vendor (contract 2, PLAN_one_model_catalog.md E2.5): applied where its runtime lists the level, lowered to the operator's cap, or dropped — and the reviewer's note says which. A contract-1 server applies none.
The model's probe report (coai-mcp --probe-api, ApiCapabilities.EffortLevels), judged per model.

thinking.note: No flag that switches codex’s thinking off has been shown taking effect, so the card says so rather than drawing a switch.
The retired Gemini CLI runtime; a row saved on it is moved to antigravity on read.
Claude’s depth is its effort (--effort); there is no separate thinking switch.
The model id carries its level (gemini-3.7-flash-high); there is no switch.
A local engine’s thinking follows its effort setting; a separate switch has not been measured.
A Team server row carries no thinking switch: contract 2 carries effort and a system prompt only.
The model’s probe report says whether its thinking can be switched off (thinkingSwitchable), per model.

fastMode.note: -c service_tier=default (Off) or =fast (On), on codex’s OWN service only — a row on another endpoint has no codex tier. Measured 2026-10-07: the key is read and checked per model; a value the model does not advertise is dropped with a warning, never a refusal.
The retired Gemini CLI runtime; a row saved on it is moved to antigravity on read.

--settings with a one-key file, fastMode true or false (documented for claude -p, v2.1.205+), Opus 5.5, 5 and 4.8 only. Measured 2026-10-07: Off reports fast_mode_state off; On is held off where the account’s own preference does not allow it, and the run says so.
No fast tier: the model id carries its level.
A local engine has no service tier.
A Team server row carries no fast mode: its contract does not.
Not until a dialect’s tier is measured on a real call (xai first); the generic openai dialect serves every unnamed endpoint and gets none.
